tour.name: Hanoi Private Tour: Old Quarter, Temple of Literature, Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum & Street Food
tour.subtitle: A private day in Vietnam's thousand-year-old capital with a licensed guide and car: Ho Chi Minh's mausoleum and stilt house, the One Pillar Pagoda, the Temple of Literature, Hoan Kiem Lake, a cyclo ride through the 36 streets of the Old Quarter, egg coffee, a water puppet show and a street-food evening.

tour.overview:
Hanoi was founded as Thang Long, 'ascending dragon', in 1010, and for most of the last thousand years it has been the capital of Vietnam. It is a city of lakes, tree-lined French boulevards, Confucian temples and the crowded Old Quarter, where each street was once home to a single guild – silk, silver, paper, herbs – and still often specialises in one trade. Its street food, eaten on tiny plastic stools on the pavement, is among the best in Asia.

This private day shows the history and daily life of Hanoi with a licensed guide and a car. You visit the Ho Chi Minh complex and the Temple of Literature in the morning, have lunch, ride a cyclo through the Old Quarter, taste egg coffee by the lake, watch a water puppet show and end with a street-food dinner.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 10 hours, ending after dinner
• Start and end: your hotel in Hanoi
• Type: private tour with licensed guide, car and driver, cyclo
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy

WHAT YOU SEE
• Ba Dinh Square, the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum and stilt house.
• The One Pillar Pagoda.
• The Temple of Literature.
• Hoan Kiem Lake and Ngoc Son temple.
• The Old Quarter by cyclo.
• A water puppet show.

WHY THIS WORKS
The mausoleum opens only in the morning, so we start there; the car avoids the scooter traffic between sights, and the cyclo shows the Old Quarter at the right pace.

WHO IT SUITS
First-time visitors, food lovers and families.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you prefer landscapes, choose our Ha Long Bay or Ninh Binh day trips.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
The mausoleum is closed on Mondays and Fridays, and for maintenance for about two months each autumn; we then visit the outside and the stilt house. Respectful dress, silence and no photos are required inside.

days.name: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum, One Pillar Pagoda, Temple of Literature, Hoan Kiem Lake, a cyclo in the Old Quarter, water puppets and street food
days.description:
What to expect: the history and street life of Hanoi in one day, with a licensed guide, private car, cyclo, show and meals.

Your guide and driver collect you at your hotel at about 7:30. You start at Ba Dinh Square, where Ho Chi Minh read Vietnam's declaration of independence on 2 September 1945. You file past his embalmed body in the granite mausoleum, guarded by soldiers in white, then walk through the gardens to the yellow Presidential Palace of the French governors and the simple wooden stilt house where Ho Chi Minh chose to live and work from 1958. Nearby, the One Pillar Pagoda, first built in 1049 by an emperor after a dream, rises from a lotus pond on a single column.

At the Temple of Literature, founded in 1070 to honour Confucius and opened in 1076 as Vietnam's first university, you walk through five courtyards of gates, ponds and frangipani trees to the stone stelae carried on the backs of tortoises, engraved with the names of the doctors who passed the royal examinations from 1442 to 1779. Students still come to touch the tortoises' heads for luck before exams. After lunch at a restaurant serving northern dishes, you reach Hoan Kiem Lake, where legend says a golden turtle took back the magic sword that freed Vietnam from Chinese rule, and cross the red Huc bridge to Ngoc Son temple on its islet.

You board cyclos – bicycle rickshaws – for a slow ride through the Old Quarter, along streets named after what they sold: Hang Bac for silver, Hang Ma for paper offerings, Hang Thiec for tin. You stop at a café for egg coffee, whipped egg yolk and condensed milk over strong coffee, invented in Hanoi in 1946 when milk was scarce. At dusk you watch a water puppet show, an art born in the flooded rice fields of the Red River delta, with puppeteers hidden behind a screen standing waist-deep in water and a live traditional orchestra. You end with a street-food dinner – bun cha, the grilled pork and noodles Barack Obama shared with Anthony Bourdain, pho, nem rán spring rolls and banh mi – and are back at your hotel at about 20:30.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
07:30 – Pick-up at your hotel.
08:00 – Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum, stilt house and One Pillar Pagoda.
10:00 – Temple of Literature.
11:45 – Lunch.
13:15 – Hoan Kiem Lake and Ngoc Son temple.
14:15 – Cyclo through the Old Quarter.
15:15 – Egg coffee and free time.
17:00 – Water puppet show.
18:15 – Street-food dinner.
20:30 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Train Street, where trains pass between houses, is often closed to visitors by the police; we visit only when allowed.
• The Vietnam Museum of Ethnology or the Hoa Lo prison can replace the mausoleum on closing days.
• Crossing the street: walk slowly and steadily; the scooters flow around you.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, licensed guide, entrance fees, cyclo, egg coffee, lunch, dinner, water puppet tickets, bottled water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: alcoholic drinks, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch, dinner.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Is the mausoleum always open?
faq.answer: No. It is closed on Mondays and Fridays, opens only in the morning, and closes for about two months each autumn. On those days we see the complex from outside and add another museum.

faq.question: Are the entrance fees and show included?
faq.answer: Yes: all entrance fees, the cyclo, the water puppet show, egg coffee, lunch and dinner.

faq.question: Is street food safe?
faq.answer: Your guide chooses busy, clean stalls with fresh food. We adapt to allergies and diets, including vegetarian.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children love the cyclo, the turtle legend and the water puppets. Child seats are provided free of charge on request.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Largely. The sites are on flat ground; the cyclo needs a step up. The car drops you close to each place.

faq.question: What should we wear at the mausoleum?
faq.answer: Covered shoulders and knees, no hats inside, and silence. Bags and cameras are checked in at the entrance.

faq.question: Can we visit Train Street?
faq.answer: Only when the authorities allow it, which changes often for safety reasons. Your guide checks on the day.

faq.question: Will we be taken to shops?
faq.answer: No. There are no commission stops.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tips are appreciated in Vietnam but never required.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Light clothes, covering clothes for the mausoleum and temples, comfortable shoes, and a light jacket from December to February.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: October to December and March to April. Hanoi has a cool winter and a hot, humid summer with rain.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
